transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I've been having this issue with food. After my shifts—I work as a cashier—I keep buying these just... huge takeout orders. Like, I'll get enough burgers, fries, chicken, and desserts to feed a whole family. And then I'll just sit there and eat almost all of it by myself before I even go home.
After eating like that, do you ever do anything to try to get rid of the food or prevent weight gain, like making yourself vomit or using laxatives?

No, I don't do anything like that. I've never tried to make myself throw up or taken laxatives or anything. I just... I just eat it all and then feel terrible about it, but I don't try to get rid of it.
While you are eating like that, do you feel like you've lost control or can't stop yourself?

Yeah, I do. It's like... once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me just clicks off. Even while I'm sitting there telling myself, 'Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more,' my hands just keep reaching for the next thing. I just can't seem to stop myself once I start.
On average, how many times a week does this happen?

Well, for the last several months, it's been happening about three or four nights most weeks. Honestly, I can't even remember a week since the foreclosure calls started where I didn't do it at least once.
Do you find that these eating episodes happen specifically when you are feeling stressed or upset, or do they happen regardless of how you are feeling emotionally?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean, I know I brought up the foreclosure stuff, and that's definitely stressful, but... I haven't really noticed if it only happens when I'm upset. Sometimes it feels like it just happens regardless of how my day went. I just haven't really paid that much attention to exactly how I'm feeling right before it starts.
During these eating episodes, do you find that you eat much faster than you normally would?

I haven't really noticed, to be honest. I mean... maybe? But I'm usually just so focused on the food that I don't really pay attention to how fast I'm going. So I couldn't say for sure if it's actually faster than my normal speed or not.
During these times, do you keep eating until you feel uncomfortably or painfully full?

Yeah. Yeah, I definitely do. A lot of nights, I just... I keep going until my stomach gets really tight and starts hurting. It gets so bad that I actually have to lean the seat all the way back if I'm in my car, or just go lie completely still in bed and wait for the pain to pass.
Do you find yourself eating these large amounts of food even when you don't feel physically hungry?

Yeah, definitely. Most of the time, I'm not even hungry when it starts. Like, I might have already had a full dinner with my wife, but I still end up looking for more food. It's almost like... I don't know, like I'm just trying to shut my head off or something. But yeah, hunger doesn't really have anything to do with it.
Do you usually eat these large amounts of food alone because you feel embarrassed by how much you are eating?

Yeah, I do. I hide it because I'm just really ashamed of it. So I'll usually eat out in my car in a parking lot somewhere, or I'll wait until my wife is completely asleep. And then... I make sure to stuff all the bags and the receipts way down deep in the trash can. I just really don't want her to see how much I actually had.
